stimuli.description: Virtual Reality simulations of various learning space designs tailored to different learning styles, including variations in spatial layout, ceiling height, window size, indoor greenery, and color choices.
V-ray renderings of classroom designs, vividly demonstrating adaptive classroom designs tailored to diverse learning modes.

tables.description: Theoretical Basis for Classroom Design Factors, outlining how spatial layout, ceiling height, window size, indoor greenery, and color scheme influence cognitive performance and emotional states.
Classroom Design Parameters for Different Learning Styles, illustrating recommended design parameters tailored to Diverger, Assimilator, Accommodator, and Converger learning styles.
Simulation diagram, showing perspective views of various classroom designs created via SketchUp modeling and V-Ray rendering.

MANOVA result, presenting F-values, degrees of freedom, p-values, and effect sizes (eta-squared) for overall effects and interactions between design factors and learning styles on attention and stress.

limitations: VR technology cannot fully replicate actual social interactions or long-term exposure effects.
Future research should incorporate field observations and longitudinal studies to confirm generalizability.
Study's sample from Taiwan may reflect collectivist influences, such as a preference for group-oriented layouts.
Comparative studies across diverse national contexts are recommended to investigate relationships between learning styles and space preferences across cultures.
Future studies could utilize functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) technology to explore relationships between prefrontal cortex activation and environmental design.
